plan_a_advantages: Includes a dedicated long run focusing on sustainable pace.
Offers a broader range of session types (aerobic, hills, cross-training)
plan_b_advantages: Prioritizes threshold and hill training, directly addressing speed and trail power.
Features shorter, more intense sessions, potentially leading to greater adaptations in a shorter timeframe.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It prioritizes threshold training and hill work, which are directly correlated with improving running economy and power on technical trails – key elements for faster trail running. Plan A, while including a long run, focuses more on maintaining a moderate pace and general aerobic fitness, lacking the targeted intensity needed for significant speed gains. Plan B’s structured approach to building climbing strength and consistent aerobic effort will be more effective in translating to improved performance on challenging trails. Furthermore, the shorter, more focused sessions in Plan B minimize the risk of overtraining and allow for better recovery.
